points.description: Gives the correct order: B (least), then C, then A (most probable), i.e. BCA.
points.partial_credit: Half if the order is almost right or only partly stated (e.g. B least and A most noted but C placement unclear).

points.description: Gives a valid justification in any wording: B is a special case/subset of C and C of A (more specific to less specific), OR correct probability calculations/formulas showing P(B)<P(C)<P(A), e.g. P(B)≈0.014, P(C)≈0.28, P(A)≈0.82 or P(C)=20·P(B).
points.partial_credit: Half if justification is on the right track but vague or only partly correct (e.g. only one of the two relations, or a formula without clear comparison).

rubric.notes: Full marks: correct order BCA plus a valid justification (subset/more-specific reasoning or correct probabilities). Part marks for an almost-correct order or a vague/partial justification. No marks for a wrong order with no valid reasoning; extra incorrect remarks that don't contradict the main idea are ignored.
